chapters.title: Chapter 3

paragraphs.text: 3-1. Paiṋcakośátmiká jaeviisattá kadaliipuśpavat.
summary: Paiṋcakośátmiká jaeviisattá kadaliipuśpavat.

paragraphs.text: [The living being is the composite of five kośas (layers of mind), like a plantain flower (with its petals).]
summary: [The living being is the composite of five kośas (layers of mind), like a plantain flower (with its petals).

paragraphs.text: Purport: In pratisaiṋcara, after the citta comes into being, there ensues gradually the pervasive manifestation of mind. And in this manifestative flow we find in the unit-body that the crudest sheath or cell is the kámamaya kośa [conscious mind], subtler than this is the manomaya kośa [subconscious mind], subtler than this subconscious is the atimánasa kośa [supra-mental mind], yet subtler than this supra-mental mind is the vijiṋánamaya kośa [subliminal mind], and the subtlest of all kośas is the hirańyamaya kośa [subtle causal mind]. The crude receptacle of the unit is the annamaya kośa [physical body], which is the property of saiṋcara. The kámamaya and manomaya kośas are called the crude and subtle minds, respectively, and the other three kośas, that is, the atimánasa, vijiṋánamaya and hirańyamaya, are called the causal [or astral, or unconscious] mind collectively. The witnessing puruśa of the crude mind is called Prájiṋa, that of the subtle mind is called Taejasa, and that of the unconscious mind is called Vishva. Saiṋcara's annamaya kośa, the crude receptacle of the living unit, is called the sthula deha [crude body]. The five kośas, from the kámamaya to the hirańyamaya, are called the sukśma deha [subtle body], and the mahattattva and ahaḿtattva are called the sámánya deha [supra-causal body, i.e., the body between the hirańyamaya kośa and (till merger into) Puruśottama]. As with the plantain flower, in the case of these kośas also, subtle things are observed and understood only after removing their crude parts.
summary: Purport: In pratisaiṋcara, after the citta comes into being, there ensues gradually the pervasive manifestation of mind.
The witnessing puruśa of the crude mind is called Prájiṋa, that of the subtle mind is called Taejasa, and that of the unconscious mind is called Vishva.
As with the plantain flower, in the case of these kośas also, subtle things are observed and understood only after removing their crude parts.

paragraphs.text: 3-2. Saptalokátmakaḿ Brahmamanah.
summary: Saptalokátmakaḿ Brahmamanah.

paragraphs.text: [The Cosmic Mind is the composite of seven lokas (layers, worlds).]
summary: [The Cosmic Mind is the composite of seven lokas (layers, worlds).

paragraphs.text: Purport: The Cosmic Mind is held in seven lokas [worlds], namely bhú [physical world], bhuvah [crude mental world], svah [subtle mental world], mahah [supra-mental world], janah [subliminal world], tapah and Satya. Puruśottama Himself, who is the witnessing entity of the Cosmic Mahattattva and Ahaḿtattva, is known as the Satyaloka. He is also called the Causal Cosmic Body. The cognitive puruśa (knower) of Brahma's hirańyamaya kośa [causal cosmic mind], is called Virát́a or Vaeshvánara, and the loka concerned is called the taparloka. The witnessing puruśa of Brahma's vijiṋánamaya kośa [subliminal cosmic mind] is also called Virát́a or Vaeshvánara, and the loka concerned goes by the name of janarloka. The witnessing puruśa of Brahma's atimánasa kośa [supra-mental cosmic mind] is also called Virát́a or Vaeshvánara, and the loka concerned is called the maharloka. The collective name of these three kośas is “causal cosmic mind” or “subtle cosmic body”. The manomaya kośa of Brahma is called the subtle cosmic mind, and its witnessing puruśa is called Hirańyagarbha. This also falls within the scope of the subtle cosmic body, and the loka concerned is called the svarloka. The kámamaya kośa of Brahma is called the crude cosmic mind, and its witnessing puruśa is called Iishvara. This may also be called the crude cosmic body. As per degree of expression of subtlety or crudity, this kośa is called partially bhuvah [crude mental world], and partially bhúrloka [crude physical world].
summary: Purport: The Cosmic Mind is held in seven lokas [worlds], namely bhú [physical world], bhuvah [crude mental world], svah [subtle mental world], mahah [supra-mental world], janah [subliminal world], tapah and Satya.
The collective name of these three kośas is “causal cosmic mind” or “subtle cosmic body”.
As per degree of expression of subtlety or crudity, this kośa is called partially bhuvah [crude mental world], and partially bhúrloka [crude physical world].

paragraphs.text: 3-3. Kárańamanasi diirghanidrá marańam.
summary: Kárańamanasi diirghanidrá marańam.

paragraphs.text: [Long sleep in the causal mind is death.]
summary: [Long sleep in the causal mind is death.

paragraphs.text: Purport: In wakefulness all three minds, namely, conscious, subconscious and unconscious, remain active. In dream, only the crude or conscious mind remains asleep, and the other two minds remain active. In sleep, both conscious and subconscious minds remain inactive; only the unconscious mind remains awake and does the work of the other two minds. When there occurs a vibrational disparity in the psycho-physical parallelism, the unconscious mind also becomes inactive. This state is called death.
summary: Purport: In wakefulness all three minds, namely, conscious, subconscious and unconscious, remain active.
In sleep, both conscious and subconscious minds remain inactive; only the unconscious mind remains awake and does the work of the other two minds.
This state is called death.

paragraphs.text: 3-4. Manovikrtih vipákápekśitá saḿskárah.
summary: Manovikrtih vipákápekśitá saḿskárah.

paragraphs.text: [A distortion of the mind-stuff waiting for expression (i.e., a reaction in potentiality) is known as a saḿskára.]
summary: [A distortion of the mind-stuff waiting for expression (i.
, a reaction in potentiality) is known as a saḿskára.
, a reaction in potentiality) is known as a saḿskára.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Virtuous or non-virtuous, whatever the act be, it begets a sort of mental distortion. The mind, however, regains its normal composure through vipáka, that is, after undergoing the consequences of one's good or bad deeds. Where action has taken place, but the consequences thereof have not been gone through or served, that is, the vipáka has been kept in abeyance, such suspended or deferred vipáka is called saḿskára [reaction in its potentiality].
summary: Purport: Virtuous or non-virtuous, whatever the act be, it begets a sort of mental distortion.
The mind, however, regains its normal composure through vipáka, that is, after undergoing the consequences of one's good or bad deeds.

Where action has taken place, but the consequences thereof have not been gone through or served, that is, the vipáka has been kept in abeyance, such suspended or deferred vipáka is called saḿskára [reaction in its potentiality].

paragraphs.text: According to the nature of the saḿskáras held in the causal, or unconscious, mind at the time of death, Prakrti, in order to get those saḿskáras served through vipáka, effects the contact of the bodiless minds with living structures ( 1 ) in the wombs of different beings – living structures that have parallelism with those bodiless minds' saḿskára-determined mental waves. This we call the rebirth of the unit concerned. One generally goes away after death with saḿskáras in accordance with one's deeds performed during one's lifetime.
summary: According to the nature of the saḿskáras held in the causal, or unconscious, mind at the time of death, Prakrti, in order to get those saḿskáras served through vipáka, effects the contact of the bodiless minds with living structures ( 1 ) in the wombs of different beings – living structures that have parallelism with those bodiless minds' saḿskára-determined mental waves.
This we call the rebirth of the unit concerned.
One generally goes away after death with saḿskáras in accordance with one's deeds performed during one's lifetime.

paragraphs.text: 3-5. Videhiimánase na kartrtvaḿ na sukháni na duhkháni.
summary: Videhiimánase na kartrtvaḿ na sukháni na duhkháni.
paragraphs.sutraRoman: Videhiimánase na kartrtvaḿ na sukháni na duhkháni
paragraphs.devanagari: विदेहीमानसे न कर्तृत्वं न सुखानि न दुह्खानि॥
paragraphs.bangla: বিদেহীমানসে ন কর্তৃত্বং ন সুখানি ন দুহ্খানি॥
paragraphs.oriya: ଵିଦେହୀମାନସେ ନ କର୍ତୃତ୍ଵଂ ନ ସୁଖାନି ନ ଦୁହ୍ଖାନି॥
paragraphs.punjabi: ਵਿਦੇਹੀਮਾਨਸੇ ਨ ਕਰ੍ਤृਤ੍ਵਂ ਨ ਸੁਖਾਨਿ ਨ ਦੁਹ੍ਖਾਨਿ॥
paragraphs.kannada: ವಿದೇಹೀಮಾನಸೇ ನ ಕರ್ತೃತ್ವಂ ನ ಸುಖಾನಿ ನ ದುಹ್ಖಾನಿ॥

paragraphs.text: [In the bodiless mind there is no doership, no feeling of pleasure or pain.]
summary: [In the bodiless mind there is no doership, no feeling of pleasure or pain.

paragraphs.text: Purport: After the separation of the mind from the body, that is, after death, the sense of weal or woe cannot exist in the unit, because for perception of pleasure and pain cerebral nerve cells and, partially, nerve fibres are necessary (which the bodiless minds do not have after death); and so the popular dogmas and beliefs that So-and-so's bodiless soul will be happy with such-and-such observances, or be unhappy and miserable with such-and-such acts, or will satisfy its revengeful propensities, are utterly and completely wrong.
summary: Purport: After the separation of the mind from the body, that is, after death, the sense of weal or woe cannot exist in the unit, because for perception of pleasure and pain cerebral nerve cells and, partially, nerve fibres are necessary (which the bodiless minds do not have after death); and so the popular dogmas and beliefs that So-and-so's bodiless soul will be happy with such-and-such observances, or be unhappy and miserable with such-and-such acts, or will satisfy its revengeful propensities, are utterly and completely wrong.

paragraphs.text: 3-6. Abhibhávanát cittáńusrśt́apretadarshanam.
summary: Abhibhávanát cittáńusrśt́apretadarshanam.

paragraphs.text: [The sight of ghosts is created by the cittáńu (mind-stuff) in concentrated thought.]
summary: [The sight of ghosts is created by the cittáńu (mind-stuff) in concentrated thought.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Actually spirits and ghosts do not exist. When in a frightened or indignant or hypnotic state a person attains temporary concentration of the mind, his or her mind-stuff takes the form of the object imagined. In such a state one sees the vision of one's thought without as well. Thinking about ghosts and spirits in solitude, he or she sees them also in the open. The external vision of the internal thought may be termed as positive hallucination. Conversely, in such a state of mind even the actually existent object may appear as non-existent. This we may call negative hallucination. Those that say that they have seen a ghost do not lie. Only the delusion of the mind appears to them as visual perception.
summary: Purport: Actually spirits and ghosts do not exist.
The external vision of the internal thought may be termed as positive hallucination.
Only the delusion of the mind appears to them as visual perception.

paragraphs.text: If hypnosis be thoroughly introspective, one may mistake one's own entity for a spirit or ghost. In such an event the person behaves in such a manner that people start saying that So-and-so is possessed by a spirit. Theomania or theophanic possession is also of the same variety.
summary: If hypnosis be thoroughly introspective, one may mistake one's own entity for a spirit or ghost.
In such an event the person behaves in such a manner that people start saying that So-and-so is possessed by a spirit.
Theomania or theophanic possession is also of the same variety.

paragraphs.text: 3-7. Hitaeśańápreśito'pavargah.
summary: Hitaeśańápreśito'pavargah.

paragraphs.text: [The requital of an action is guided by the (divine) longing for welfare.]
summary: [The requital of an action is guided by the (divine) longing for welfare.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Even behind the requital of an act (the fruits that follow the completion of an act) lies the divine desire of benevolence. The punishment for an evil act teaches one to keep away from evil doings. The reward for a good and benevolent act teaches people that they will never get such a reward if ever they commit an evil act.
summary: Purport: Even behind the requital of an act (the fruits that follow the completion of an act) lies the divine desire of benevolence.
The punishment for an evil act teaches one to keep away from evil doings.
The reward for a good and benevolent act teaches people that they will never get such a reward if ever they commit an evil act.

paragraphs.text: 3-8. Muktyákáunkśayá sadgurupráptih.
summary: Muktyákáunkśayá sadgurupráptih.

paragraphs.text: [Out of the intense desire for mukti (liberation), one attains one's sadguru (perfect master).]
summary: [Out of the intense desire for mukti (liberation), one attains one's sadguru (perfect master).

paragraphs.text: Purport: When a vehement desire for emancipation wakes up in a person, he or she attains his or her sadguru [true spiritual preceptor] on the strength of that desire.
summary: Purport: When a vehement desire for emancipation wakes up in a person, he or she attains his or her sadguru [true spiritual preceptor] on the strength of that desire.

paragraphs.text: 3-9. Brahmaeva gururekah náparah.
summary: Brahmaeva gururekah náparah.

paragraphs.text: [Only Brahma is the guru, no one else.]
summary: [Only Brahma is the guru, no one else.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Brahma alone is the guru. Brahma alone directs the units to the path of emancipation through the media of different receptacles or bodies. No one except Brahma conforms to the real significance of the word “guru”.
summary: Purport: Brahma alone is the guru.
Brahma alone directs the units to the path of emancipation through the media of different receptacles or bodies.
No one except Brahma conforms to the real significance of the word “guru”.

paragraphs.text: 3-10. Vádhá sá yuśamáná shaktih sevyaḿ sthápayati lakśye.
summary: Vádhá sá yuśamáná shaktih sevyaḿ sthápayati lakśye.
paragraphs.sutraRoman: Vádhá sá yuśamáná shaktih sevyaḿ sthápayati lakśye
paragraphs.devanagari: वाधा सा युषमाना शक्तिः सेव्यं स्थापयति लक्ष्ये॥
paragraphs.bangla: বাধা সা যুষমানা শক্তিঃ সেব্যং স্থাপযতি লক্ষ্যে॥
paragraphs.oriya: ଵାଧା ସା ଯୁଷମାନା ଶକ୍ତିଃ ସେଵ୍ଯଂ ସ୍ଥାପଯତି ଲକ୍ଷ୍ଯେ॥
paragraphs.punjabi: ਵਾਧਾ ਸਾ ਯੁषਮਾਨਾ ਸ਼ਕ੍ਤਿਃ ਸੇਵ੍ਯਂ ਸ੍ਥਾਪਯਤਿ ਲਕ੍ष੍ਯੇ॥
paragraphs.kannada: ವಾಧಾ ಸಾ ಯುಷಮಾನಾ ಶಕ್ತಿಃ ಸೇವ್ಯಂ ಸ್ಥಾಪಯತಿ ಲಕ್ಷ್ಯೇ॥

paragraphs.text: [Obstacles are the helping forces that establish one in the goal.]
summary: [Obstacles are the helping forces that establish one in the goal.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Obstacles in fact are no foes on the path of sádhaná [spiritual practice], but indeed friends. They only do service to a person. It is on account of these obstacles that the battle rages against them, and this counter-effort alone carries the sádhaka [spiritual aspirant] to his or her cherished goal.
summary: Purport: Obstacles in fact are no foes on the path of sádhaná [spiritual practice], but indeed friends.
They only do service to a person.
It is on account of these obstacles that the battle rages against them, and this counter-effort alone carries the sádhaka [spiritual aspirant] to his or her cherished goal.

paragraphs.text: 3-11. Prárthanárcaná mátraeva bhramamúlam.
summary: Prárthanárcaná mátraeva bhramamúlam.

paragraphs.text: [Prayer and ritualistic worship become a source of confusion.]
summary: [Prayer and ritualistic worship become a source of confusion.

paragraphs.text: Purport: It is useless to pray to God for something, for He is sure to give what is necessary. Solicitation or importunity in the name of worship is nothing but toadyism and flattery.
summary: Purport: It is useless to pray to God for something, for He is sure to give what is necessary.
Solicitation or importunity in the name of worship is nothing but toadyism and flattery.
Solicitation or importunity in the name of worship is nothing but toadyism and flattery.

paragraphs.text: 3-12. Bhaktirbhagavadbhávaná na stutirnárcaná.
summary: Bhaktirbhagavadbhávaná na stutirnárcaná.

paragraphs.text: [Devotion is ideation on God, not flattery of God or ritualistic worship.]
summary: [Devotion is ideation on God, not flattery of God or ritualistic worship.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Being merged in the constant thought of God is devotion. Devotion is not related to the chanting of hymns or ritualistic worship with different paraphernalia. A devotee may perform these, but they are not an indispensable part of devotional sádhaná.
summary: Purport: Being merged in the constant thought of God is devotion.
Devotion is not related to the chanting of hymns or ritualistic worship with different paraphernalia.
A devotee may perform these, but they are not an indispensable part of devotional sádhaná.

chapters.title: Chapter 4

paragraphs.text: 4-1. Triguńátmiká srśt́imátrká asheśatrikońadhárá.
summary: Triguńátmiká srśt́imátrká asheśatrikońadhárá.

paragraphs.text: [The tri-attributional primordial force (progenitrix of creation) flows on in endless triangular forms.]
summary: [The tri-attributional primordial force (progenitrix of creation) flows on in endless triangular forms.

paragraphs.text: Purport: In Parama Puruśa a countless number of linear waves are taking place in the different flows of sattva [sentient], rajah [mutative] and tamah [static]. Their triple-attributional flows go on evolving triangles or different other multi-conical or polygonal diagrams. Even these polygonal diagrams are gradually getting transformed into triangles due to svarúpa parińáma [homomorphic evolution]. This triple-qualitative mátrkáshakti [primordial force] is endless.
summary: Purport: In Parama Puruśa a countless number of linear waves are taking place in the different flows of sattva [sentient], rajah [mutative] and tamah [static].
Even these polygonal diagrams are gradually getting transformed into triangles due to svarúpa parińáma [homomorphic evolution].
This triple-qualitative mátrkáshakti [primordial force] is endless.

paragraphs.text: 4-2. Tribhúje Sá svarúpaparińámátmiká.
summary: Tribhúje Sá svarúpaparińámátmiká.

paragraphs.text: [In the triangle of forces, the three attributes of Prakrti are locked in endless mutual transformation.]
summary: [In the triangle of forces, the three attributes of Prakrti are locked in endless mutual transformation.

paragraphs.text: Purport: In these triangles transformations of sattva into rajah, rajah into tamah, then again of tamah into rajah and rajah into sattva, have been going on back and forth endlessly. These transformations are called svarúpa parińáma [homomorphic evolution].
summary: Purport: In these triangles transformations of sattva into rajah, rajah into tamah, then again of tamah into rajah and rajah into sattva, have been going on back and forth endlessly.
These transformations are called svarúpa parińáma [homomorphic evolution].
These transformations are called svarúpa parińáma [homomorphic evolution].

paragraphs.text: 4-3. Prathamá avyakte Sá Shivánii kendre ca Paramashivah.
summary: Prathamá avyakte Sá Shivánii kendre ca Paramashivah.
paragraphs.sutraRoman: Prathamá avyakte Sá Shivánii kendre ca Paramashivah
paragraphs.devanagari: प्रथमा अव्यक्ते सा शिवानी केन्द्रे च परमशिवः॥
paragraphs.bangla: প্রথমা অব্যক্তে সা শিবানী কেন্দ্রে চ পরমশিবঃ॥
paragraphs.oriya: ପ୍ରଥମା ଅଵ୍ଯକ୍ତେ ସା ଶିଵାନୀ କେନ୍ଦ୍ରେ ଚ ପରମଶିଵଃ॥
paragraphs.punjabi: ਪ੍ਰਥਮਾ ਅਵ੍ਯਕ੍ਤੇ ਸਾ ਸ਼ਿਵਾਨੀ ਕੇਨ੍ਦ੍ਰੇ ਚ ਪਰਮਸ਼ਿਵਃ॥
paragraphs.kannada: ಪ್ರಥಮಾ ಅವ್ಯಕ್ತೇ ಸಾ ಶಿವಾನೀ ಕೇನ್ದ್ರೇ ಚ ಪರಮಶಿವಃ॥

paragraphs.text: [In the first stage (not yet a stage of actual manifestation), Prakrti is called Shivánii, and the witnessing Puruśa at the nucleus is called Paramashiva.]
summary: [In the first stage (not yet a stage of actual manifestation), Prakrti is called Shivánii, and the witnessing Puruśa at the nucleus is called Paramashiva.

paragraphs.text: Purport: The thread wherewith the mid-points of these triangles are interwoven is Puruśottama, or Paramashiva. So long as these triangles do not lose their equipoise in the wake of developing forces, we may regard it as the initial stage of the triangular receptacles. This first stage is verily the pre-evolutional stage and hence it is purely a theoretical stage. Prakrti, the creatress of these initial receptacles, is called Shivánii or Kaośikii, and the witnessing Puruśa is called Shiva.
summary: Purport: The thread wherewith the mid-points of these triangles are interwoven is Puruśottama, or Paramashiva.
This first stage is verily the pre-evolutional stage and hence it is purely a theoretical stage.
Prakrti, the creatress of these initial receptacles, is called Shivánii or Kaośikii, and the witnessing Puruśa is called Shiva.

paragraphs.text: 4-4. Dvitiiyá sakale prathamodgame Bhaeravii Bhaeraváshritá.
summary: Dvitiiyá sakale prathamodgame Bhaeravii Bhaeraváshritá.

paragraphs.text: [In the second phase, when the germ of evolution sprouts, Prakrti is called Bhaeravii, and the witnessing Puruśa is called Bhaerava.]
summary: [In the second phase, when the germ of evolution sprouts, Prakrti is called Bhaeravii, and the witnessing Puruśa is called Bhaerava.

paragraphs.text: Purport: With the loss of equipoise of the triangle, the germ of evolution sprouts forth from any of the vertices and moves forward as a straight line as per degrees of the guńas. This state is really the manifested state of Puruśa and Prakrti. Here Puruśa is saguńa [qualified], for Prakrti has got the opportunity of expressing Herself. Prakrti the creatress of this state is called Bhaeravii shakti, and the name of the witnessing Puruśa is Bhaerava.
summary: Purport: With the loss of equipoise of the triangle, the germ of evolution sprouts forth from any of the vertices and moves forward as a straight line as per degrees of the guńas.
Here Puruśa is saguńa [qualified], for Prakrti has got the opportunity of expressing Herself.
Prakrti the creatress of this state is called Bhaeravii shakti, and the name of the witnessing Puruśa is Bhaerava.

paragraphs.text: 4-5. Sadrshaparińámena Bhavánii Sá Bhavadárá.
summary: Sadrshaparińámena Bhavánii Sá Bhavadárá.

paragraphs.text: [In the vibrational world there is a sequence of similarity of curvatures (homogenesis). Here Prakrti is called Bhavánii and the witnessing Puruśa is called Bhava.]
summary: [In the vibrational world there is a sequence of similarity of curvatures (homogenesis).
Here Prakrti is called Bhavánii and the witnessing Puruśa is called Bhava.
Here Prakrti is called Bhavánii and the witnessing Puruśa is called Bhava.

paragraphs.text: Purport: In time as the result of internal clashes the flow of forces betrays some curvatures, and the density of the Puruśabháva [stance of Consciousness] also goes on decreasing. In this very condition develops the first kalá [curvature]. The second kalá is similar (not identical) to the first, and the third is similar to the second, and so on. So goes the kalá praváha [sequential or phasic flow]. This sequential evolution of kalás is called sadrsha parińáma [homogenesis, or similitude]. In these homogenetic waves are evolved the mental and physical worlds. It is due to this (homoform) curvilinear evolution that we find that the child of a human is a human and tree begets tree. The kalás are similar but not identical, and so although the difference between two successive kalás is not clearly perceivable, the differences of kalás having distant mutual relations are clearly understandable. Although the physical changes of one whom we see every day are not understandable, we can certainly make out the difference if we see a child of five, after twenty years, as a youth of twenty-five. Although human begets human, there will be a gulf of difference between a human of a million years ago and a human of today. In fact the creatress of the manifest world is this sequential force, which is called Bhavánii shakti and whose witnessing Puruśa is Bhava. The word bhava means “creation”.
summary: Purport: In time as the result of internal clashes the flow of forces betrays some curvatures, and the density of the Puruśabháva [stance of Consciousness] also goes on decreasing.
It is due to this (homoform) curvilinear evolution that we find that the child of a human is a human and tree begets tree.
The word bhava means “creation”.

paragraphs.text: 4-6. Shambhúliuṋgát tasya vyaktih.
summary: Shambhúliuṋgát tasya vyaktih.

paragraphs.text: [The process of creation starts from Shambhúliuṋga.]
summary: [The process of creation starts from Shambhúliuṋga.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Actually the evolution from the theoretical stage to the practical manifestation dates from the very first expression of Bhavánii emanating from one of the points of the triangular receptacle. The common point of the theoretical and the practical evolution is called Shambhúliuṋga [Puruśa at the vertex of the triangle, the source of saiṋcara]. Actually this Shambhúliuṋga is the root-point of the fundamental positivity, after which comes the náda [flow without any curvature], followed by kalá.
summary: Purport: Actually the evolution from the theoretical stage to the practical manifestation dates from the very first expression of Bhavánii emanating from one of the points of the triangular receptacle.
The common point of the theoretical and the practical evolution is called Shambhúliuṋga [Puruśa at the vertex of the triangle, the source of saiṋcara].
Actually this Shambhúliuṋga is the root-point of the fundamental positivity, after which comes the náda [flow without any curvature], followed by kalá.

paragraphs.text: 4-7. Sthúliibhavane nidritá sá kuńd́alinii.
summary: Sthúliibhavane nidritá sá kuńd́alinii.

paragraphs.text: [In the ultimate state of crudification, the paráshakti lying dormant at Svayambhúliuṋga is called the kuńd́alinii (“coiled serpentine”).]
summary: [In the ultimate state of crudification, the paráshakti lying dormant at Svayambhúliuṋga is called the kuńd́alinii (“coiled serpentine”).

paragraphs.text: Purport: The last expressional point, which is the fringe of the Bhavánii shakti, is the ultimate state of expression of force – the ultimate state of crudity. In this state of crudity the paráshakti [introversial pervasive force] that is lying in a quiescent state as the jiivabháva [finite subjectivity], is called the kulakuńd́alinii [“coiled serpentine”, or force of fundamental negativity].
summary: Purport: The last expressional point, which is the fringe of the Bhavánii shakti, is the ultimate state of expression of force – the ultimate state of crudity.

In this state of crudity the paráshakti [introversial pervasive force] that is lying in a quiescent state as the jiivabháva [finite subjectivity], is called the kulakuńd́alinii [“coiled serpentine”, or force of fundamental negativity].

In this state of crudity the paráshakti [introversial pervasive force] that is lying in a quiescent state as the jiivabháva [finite subjectivity], is called the kulakuńd́alinii [“coiled serpentine”, or force of fundamental negativity].

paragraphs.text: 4-8. Kuńd́alinii sá múliibhútá rńátmiká.
summary: Kuńd́alinii sá múliibhútá rńátmiká.

paragraphs.text: [The kuńd́alinii is the (force of) fundamental negativity.]
summary: [The kuńd́alinii is the (force of) fundamental negativity.

paragraphs.text: Purport: The ultimate point of manifestation is called Svayambhúliuṋga. Svayambhúliuṋga is the ultimate point of negativity, wherein resides the kulakuńd́alinii force, quiescent and coiled like a serpent. If Shambhúliuṋga be the fundamental positivity, then the kulakuńd́alinii, lying at Svayambhúliuṋga, we may call the force of fundamental negativity.

Svayambhúliuṋga is the ultimate point of negativity, wherein resides the kulakuńd́alinii force, quiescent and coiled like a serpent.

chapters.title: Chapter 5

paragraphs.text: 5-1. Varńapradhánatá cakradháráyám.
summary: Varńapradhánatá cakradháráyám.

paragraphs.text: [In the movement of the social cycle, one class is always dominant.]
summary: [In the movement of the social cycle, one class is always dominant.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Since no well-knit social order had evolved in the distant past, we may call that age the Shúdra Age; in those days all people survived by their manual labour. Then came the age of clan leaders – the age of the strong and the brave – which we may call the Kśatriya Age. This was followed by the age of intellectuals, which we may call the Vipra Age. Finally came the age of capitalists, the Vaeshya Age.
summary: Purport: Since no well-knit social order had evolved in the distant past, we may call that age the Shúdra Age; in those days all people survived by their manual labour.
This was followed by the age of intellectuals, which we may call the Vipra Age.
Finally came the age of capitalists, the Vaeshya Age.

paragraphs.text: When the warriors and intellectuals are reduced to the level of manual labourers as a result of exploitation during the Vaeshya Age, shúdra revolution occurs. The shúdras have neither a well-knit social order nor sufficient intellect to govern society. Hence, the post-capitalist administration passes into the hands of those who provide the leadership in the shúdra revolution. These people are brave and courageous, so they begin the second Kśatriya Age.
summary: When the warriors and intellectuals are reduced to the level of manual labourers as a result of exploitation during the Vaeshya Age, shúdra revolution occurs.
Hence, the post-capitalist administration passes into the hands of those who provide the leadership in the shúdra revolution.
These people are brave and courageous, so they begin the second Kśatriya Age.

paragraphs.text: In this way the Shúdra, Kśatriya, Vipra and Vaeshya Ages move in succession, followed by revolution; then the second cyclic order begins. Thus, the rotation of the samája cakra [social cycle] continues.
summary: In this way the Shúdra, Kśatriya, Vipra and Vaeshya Ages move in succession, followed by revolution; then the second cyclic order begins.
Thus, the rotation of the samája cakra [social cycle] continues.
Thus, the rotation of the samája cakra [social cycle] continues.

paragraphs.text: 5-2. Cakrakendre sadvipráh cakraniyantrakáh.
summary: Cakrakendre sadvipráh cakraniyantrakáh.

paragraphs.text: [Located in the nucleus of the social cycle, sadvipras control the social cycle.]
summary: [Located in the nucleus of the social cycle, sadvipras control the social cycle.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Those who are staunch moralists and sincere spiritualists, and who want to put an end to immorality and exploitation by the application of force, are called sadvipras. They do not belong to the periphery of the social cycle because they are to control society remaining firmly established in the nucleus of the social cycle.
summary: Purport: Those who are staunch moralists and sincere spiritualists, and who want to put an end to immorality and exploitation by the application of force, are called sadvipras.
They do not belong to the periphery of the social cycle because they are to control society remaining firmly established in the nucleus of the social cycle.
They do not belong to the periphery of the social cycle because they are to control society remaining firmly established in the nucleus of the social cycle.

paragraphs.text: The social cycle will no doubt rotate, but if, due to their dominance, the warriors in the Kśatriya Age, the intellectuals in the Vipra Age or the capitalists in the Vaeshya Age degenerate into rapacious exploiters instead of functioning as benevolent administrators, the sacred duty of the sadvipras shall be to protect the righteous and the exploited and subdue the wicked and the exploiters through the application of force.
summary: The social cycle will no doubt rotate, but if, due to their dominance, the warriors in the Kśatriya Age, the intellectuals in the Vipra Age or the capitalists in the Vaeshya Age degenerate into rapacious exploiters instead of functioning as benevolent administrators, the sacred duty of the sadvipras shall be to protect the righteous and the exploited and subdue the wicked and the exploiters through the application of force.

paragraphs.text: 5-3. Shaktisampátena cakragativardhanaḿ krántih.
summary: Shaktisampátena cakragativardhanaḿ krántih.

paragraphs.text: [Accelerating the movement of the social cycle by the application of force is called “evolution”.]
summary: [Accelerating the movement of the social cycle by the application of force is called “evolution”.

paragraphs.text: Purport: When warriors degenerate into exploiters, sadvipras will establish the Vipra Age by subduing the exploiting warriors. Consequently, the advent of the Vipra Age, which should have occurred through a natural process, is expedited by the application of force. A change of ages in this way may be called kránti [“evolution”]. The difference between evolution and svábhávika parivarttana [natural change] is only this: in evolution the movement of the social cycle is accelerated by the application of force.
summary: Purport: When warriors degenerate into exploiters, sadvipras will establish the Vipra Age by subduing the exploiting warriors.
A change of ages in this way may be called kránti [“evolution”].
The difference between evolution and svábhávika parivarttana [natural change] is only this: in evolution the movement of the social cycle is accelerated by the application of force.

paragraphs.text: 5-4. Tiivrashaktisampátena gativardhanaḿ viplavah.
summary: Tiivrashaktisampátena gativardhanaḿ viplavah.

paragraphs.text: [Accelerating the movement of the social cycle by the application of tremendous force is called “revolution”.]
summary: [Accelerating the movement of the social cycle by the application of tremendous force is called “revolution”.

paragraphs.text: Purport: When a particular age is replaced by the successive age within a short time, or when the application of tremendous force is necessary to destroy the entrenched hegemony of a particular age, then such change is called viplava [“revolution”].
summary: Purport: When a particular age is replaced by the successive age within a short time, or when the application of tremendous force is necessary to destroy the entrenched hegemony of a particular age, then such change is called viplava [“revolution”].

paragraphs.text: 5-5. Shaktisampátena vipariitadháráyáḿ vikrántih.
summary: Shaktisampátena vipariitadháráyáḿ vikrántih.

paragraphs.text: [Reversing the movement of the social cycle by the application of force is called “counter-evolution”.]
summary: [Reversing the movement of the social cycle by the application of force is called “counter-evolution”.

paragraphs.text: Purport: If any age reverts to the preceding one by the application of force, such a change is called vikránti [“counter-evolution”]. For instance, the establishment of the Kśatriya Age after the Vipra Age is counter-evolution. This counter-evolution is extremely short-lived. That is, within a very short time this age is again replaced by the next age or the one after it. In other words, if the Kśatriya Age suddenly supersedes the Vipra Age through counter-evolution, then the Kśatriya Age will not last long. Within a short time either the Vipra Age, or as a natural concomitant the Vaeshya Age, will follow.
summary: Purport: If any age reverts to the preceding one by the application of force, such a change is called vikránti [“counter-evolution”].
That is, within a very short time this age is again replaced by the next age or the one after it.
Within a short time either the Vipra Age, or as a natural concomitant the Vaeshya Age, will follow.

paragraphs.text: 5-6. Tiivrashaktisampátena vipariitadháráyaḿ prativiplavah.
summary: Tiivrashaktisampátena vipariitadháráyaḿ prativiplavah.

paragraphs.text: [Reversing the movement of the social cycle by the application of tremendous force is called “counter-revolution”.]
summary: [Reversing the movement of the social cycle by the application of tremendous force is called “counter-revolution”.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Likewise, if within a very short time the social cycle is turned backwards by the application of tremendous force, such a change is called prativiplava [“counter-revolution”]. Counter-revolution is even more short-lived than counter-evolution.
summary: Purport: Likewise, if within a very short time the social cycle is turned backwards by the application of tremendous force, such a change is called prativiplava [“counter-revolution”].
Counter-revolution is even more short-lived than counter-evolution.
Counter-revolution is even more short-lived than counter-evolution.

paragraphs.text: 5-7. Púrńávartanena parikrántih.
summary: Púrńávartanena parikrántih.

paragraphs.text: [A complete rotation of the social cycle is called “peripheric evolution”.]
summary: [A complete rotation of the social cycle is called “peripheric evolution”.

paragraphs.text: Purport: One complete rotation of the social cycle, concluding with shúdra revolution, is called parikránti [“peripheric evolution”].
summary: Purport: One complete rotation of the social cycle, concluding with shúdra revolution, is called parikránti [“peripheric evolution”].

paragraphs.text: 5-8. Vaecitryaḿ prákrtadharmah samánaḿ na bhaviśyati.
summary: Vaecitryaḿ prákrtadharmah samánaḿ na bhaviśyati.

paragraphs.text: [Diversity, not identity, is the law of nature.]
summary: [Diversity, not identity, is the law of nature.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Diversity, not identity, is the innate characteristic of the Supreme Operative Principle. No two objects in the universe are identical, nor two bodies, two minds, two molecules or two atoms. This diversity is the inherent tendency of the Supreme Operative Principle.
summary: Purport: Diversity, not identity, is the innate characteristic of the Supreme Operative Principle.
No two objects in the universe are identical, nor two bodies, two minds, two molecules or two atoms.
This diversity is the inherent tendency of the Supreme Operative Principle.

paragraphs.text: Those who want to make everything equal are sure to fail because they are going against the innate characteristic of the Supreme Operative Principle. All things are equal only in the unmanifest state of the Supreme Operative Principle. Those who think of making all things equal inevitably think of the destruction of everything.
summary: Those who want to make everything equal are sure to fail because they are going against the innate characteristic of the Supreme Operative Principle.
All things are equal only in the unmanifest state of the Supreme Operative Principle.
Those who think of making all things equal inevitably think of the destruction of everything.

paragraphs.text: 5-9. Yugasya sarvanimnaprayojanaḿ sarveśáḿ vidheyam.
summary: Yugasya sarvanimnaprayojanaḿ sarveśáḿ vidheyam.

paragraphs.text: [The minimum requirements of an age should be guaranteed to all.]
summary: [The minimum requirements of an age should be guaranteed to all.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Hararme pitá Gaorii mátá svadeshah bhuvanatrayam. That is, “Supreme Consciousness is my father, the Supreme Operative Principle is my mother, and the three worlds are my homeland.” The entire wealth of the universe is the common patrimony of all, though no two things in the universe are absolutely equal. So the minimum requirements of life should be made available to everybody. In other words, food, clothing, medical treatment, housing and education must be provided to all. The minimum requirements of human beings, however, change according to the change in ages. For instance, for conveyance the minimum requirement may be a bicycle in one age and an aeroplane in another age. The minimum requirements must be provided for all people according to the age in which they live.
summary: Purport: Hararme pitá Gaorii mátá svadeshah bhuvanatrayam.
In other words, food, clothing, medical treatment, housing and education must be provided to all.
The minimum requirements must be provided for all people according to the age in which they live.

paragraphs.text: 5-10. Atiriktaḿ pradátavyaḿ guńánupátena.
summary: Atiriktaḿ pradátavyaḿ guńánupátena.

paragraphs.text: [The surplus wealth should be distributed among meritorious people according to the degree of their merit.]
summary: [The surplus wealth should be distributed among meritorious people according to the degree of their merit.

paragraphs.text: Purport: After meeting the minimum requirements of all in any age, the surplus wealth will have to be distributed among meritorious people according to the degree of their merit. In an age when a bicycle is the minimum requirement for common people, a motor vehicle is necessary for a physician. In recognition of people's merit, and to provide the meritorious with greater opportunities to serve the society, they have to be provided with motor vehicles. The dictum “Serve according to your capacity and earn according to your necessity” sounds pleasing, but will yield no results in the hard soil of the earth. ( 1 )
summary: Purport: After meeting the minimum requirements of all in any age, the surplus wealth will have to be distributed among meritorious people according to the degree of their merit.
In recognition of people's merit, and to provide the meritorious with greater opportunities to serve the society, they have to be provided with motor vehicles.
The dictum “Serve according to your capacity and earn according to your necessity” sounds pleasing, but will yield no results in the hard soil of the earth.

paragraphs.text: 5-11. Sarvanimnamánavardhanaḿ samájajiivalakśańam.
summary: Sarvanimnamánavardhanaḿ samájajiivalakśańam.

paragraphs.text: [Increasing the minimum standard of living of the people is the indication of the vitality of society.]
summary: [Increasing the minimum standard of living of the people is the indication of the vitality of society.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Meritorious people should receive more than the amount of minimum requirements allocated to people in general, and there should be ceaseless efforts to raise the minimum standard of living. For instance, today common people need bicycles whereas meritorious people need motor vehicles, but a proper effort should be made to provide common people with motor vehicles. After everybody has been provided with a motor vehicle, it may be necessary to provide each meritorious person with an aeroplane. After providing every meritorious person with an aeroplane, efforts should also be made to provide every common person with an aeroplane, raising the minimum standard of living. In this way efforts to raise the minimum standard of living will have to go on endlessly, and on this endeavour will depend the mundane development and prosperity of human beings.
summary: Purport: Meritorious people should receive more than the amount of minimum requirements allocated to people in general, and there should be ceaseless efforts to raise the minimum standard of living.
After everybody has been provided with a motor vehicle, it may be necessary to provide each meritorious person with an aeroplane.
In this way efforts to raise the minimum standard of living will have to go on endlessly, and on this endeavour will depend the mundane development and prosperity of human beings.

paragraphs.text: 5-12. Samájádeshena viná dhanasaiṋcayah akartavyah. ( 2 )
summary: Samájádeshena viná dhanasaiṋcayah akartavyah.

paragraphs.text: [No individual should be allowed to accumulate any physical wealth without the clear permission or approval of the collective body.]
summary: [No individual should be allowed to accumulate any physical wealth without the clear permission or approval of the collective body.

paragraphs.text: Purport: The universe is the collective property of all. All people have usufructuary rights but no one has the right to misuse this collective property. If a person acquires and accumulates excessive wealth, he or she directly curtails the happiness and convenience of others in society. Such behaviour is flagrantly antisocial. Therefore, no one should be allowed to accumulate wealth without the permission of society.
summary: Purport: The universe is the collective property of all.
If a person acquires and accumulates excessive wealth, he or she directly curtails the happiness and convenience of others in society.
Therefore, no one should be allowed to accumulate wealth without the permission of society.

paragraphs.text: 5-13. Sthúlasúkśmakárańeśu caramopayogah prakartavyah vicárasamarthitaḿ vańt́anaiṋca.
summary: Sthúlasúkśmakárańeśu caramopayogah prakartavyah vicárasamarthitaḿ vańt́anaiṋca.

paragraphs.text: [There should be maximum utilization and rational distribution of all mundane, supramundane and spiritual potentialities of the universe.]
summary: [There should be maximum utilization and rational distribution of all mundane, supramundane and spiritual potentialities of the universe.

paragraphs.text: Purport: The wealth and resources available in the crude, subtle and causal worlds should be developed for the welfare of all. All resources hidden in the quinquelemental world – solid, liquid, luminous, aerial and ethereal – should be fully utilized, and the endeavour to do this will ensure the maximum development of the universe. People will have to earnestly explore land, sea and space to discover, extract and process the raw materials needed for their requirements.
summary: Purport: The wealth and resources available in the crude, subtle and causal worlds should be developed for the welfare of all.

All resources hidden in the quinquelemental world – solid, liquid, luminous, aerial and ethereal – should be fully utilized, and the endeavour to do this will ensure the maximum development of the universe.
People will have to earnestly explore land, sea and space to discover, extract and process the raw materials needed for their requirements.

paragraphs.text: There should be rational distribution of the accumulated wealth of humanity. In other words, all people must be guaranteed the minimum requirements. In addition, the requirements of meritorious people, and in certain cases those with special needs, will also have to be kept in mind.
summary: There should be rational distribution of the accumulated wealth of humanity.
In other words, all people must be guaranteed the minimum requirements.
In addition, the requirements of meritorious people, and in certain cases those with special needs, will also have to be kept in mind.

paragraphs.text: 5-14. Vyaśt́isamaśt́isháriiramánasádhyátmikasambhávanáyáḿ caramo'payogashca.
summary: Vyaśt́isamaśt́isháriiramánasádhyátmikasambhávanáyáḿ caramo'payogashca.

paragraphs.text: [There should be maximum utilization of the physical, metaphysical and spiritual potentialities of unit and collective bodies of human society.]
summary: [There should be maximum utilization of the physical, metaphysical and spiritual potentialities of unit and collective bodies of human society.

paragraphs.text: Purport: Society must ensure the maximum development of the collective body, collective mind and collective spirit. One must not forget that collective welfare lies in individuals and individual welfare lies in collectivity. Without ensuring individual comforts through the proper provision of food, light, air, accommodation and medical treatment, the welfare of the collective body can never be achieved. One will have to promote individual welfare motivated by the spirit of promoting collective welfare.
summary: Purport: Society must ensure the maximum development of the collective body, collective mind and collective spirit.
Without ensuring individual comforts through the proper provision of food, light, air, accommodation and medical treatment, the welfare of the collective body can never be achieved.
One will have to promote individual welfare motivated by the spirit of promoting collective welfare.

paragraphs.text: The development of the collective mind is impossible without developing proper social awareness, encouraging the spirit of social service and awakening knowledge in every individual. So, inspired with the thought of the welfare of the collective mind, one has to promote the well-being of the individual mind.
summary: The development of the collective mind is impossible without developing proper social awareness, encouraging the spirit of social service and awakening knowledge in every individual.
So, inspired with the thought of the welfare of the collective mind, one has to promote the well-being of the individual mind.
So, inspired with the thought of the welfare of the collective mind, one has to promote the well-being of the individual mind.

paragraphs.text: The absence of spiritual morality and spirituality in individuals will break the backbone of the collectivity. So for the sake of collective welfare one will have to awaken spirituality in individuals. The mere presence of a handful of strong and brave people, a small number of scholars or a few spiritualists does not indicate the progress of the entire society. The potential for infinite physical, mental and spiritual development is inherent in every human being. This potentiality has to be harnessed and brought to fruition.
summary: The absence of spiritual morality and spirituality in individuals will break the backbone of the collectivity.
The mere presence of a handful of strong and brave people, a small number of scholars or a few spiritualists does not indicate the progress of the entire society.
This potentiality has to be harnessed and brought to fruition.

paragraphs.text: 5-15. Sthúlasúkśma kárańo'payogáh susantulitáh vidheyáh.
summary: Sthúlasúkśma kárańo'payogáh susantulitáh vidheyáh.

paragraphs.text: [There should be a proper adjustment amongst these physical, metaphysical, mundane, supramundane and spiritual utilizations.]
summary: [There should be a proper adjustment amongst these physical, metaphysical, mundane, supramundane and spiritual utilizations.

paragraphs.text: Purport: While promoting individual and collective welfare, there should be proper adjustment among the physical, mental and spiritual spheres and the crude, subtle and causal worlds. For instance, society has the responsibility to meet the minimum requirements of every individual, but if it arranges food and builds a house for everyone under the impetus of this responsibility, individual initiative is retarded. People will gradually become lethargic. Therefore, society has to make arrangements so that people, in exchange for their labour according to their capacity, can earn the money they require to purchase the minimum requirements. In order to raise the level of the minimum requirements of people, the best policy is to increase their purchasing capacity.
summary: Purport: While promoting individual and collective welfare, there should be proper adjustment among the physical, mental and spiritual spheres and the crude, subtle and causal worlds.
People will gradually become lethargic.
In order to raise the level of the minimum requirements of people, the best policy is to increase their purchasing capacity.

paragraphs.text: “Proper adjustment” also means that while taking service from a person who is physically, mentally and spiritually developed, society should follow a balanced policy. Society will take physical, intellectual or spiritual service from a person depending upon which of these capacities is conspicuously developed in that person. From those who are sufficiently physically and intellectually developed, society will follow a balanced policy and accordingly take more intellectual service and less physical service, because intellectual power is comparatively subtle and rare. From those who are physically, mentally and spiritually developed, society will take maximum spiritual service, less intellectual service and still less physical service.
summary: “Proper adjustment” also means that while taking service from a person who is physically, mentally and spiritually developed, society should follow a balanced policy.

From those who are sufficiently physically and intellectually developed, society will follow a balanced policy and accordingly take more intellectual service and less physical service, because intellectual power is comparatively subtle and rare.
From those who are physically, mentally and spiritually developed, society will take maximum spiritual service, less intellectual service and still less physical service.

paragraphs.text: As far as social welfare is concerned, those endowed with spiritual power can render the greatest service, followed by those endowed with intellectual power. Those having physical power, though not negligible, cannot do anything by themselves. Whatever they do, they do under the instructions of those endowed with intellectual and spiritual power. Hence the responsibility of controlling the society should not be in the hands of those who are endowed only with physical power, or in the hands of those endowed only with courage, or in the hands of those who are developed only intellectually, or in the hands of those with worldly knowledge alone. Social control will have to be in the hands of those who are spiritually elevated, intelligent and brave all at the same time.
summary: As far as social welfare is concerned, those endowed with spiritual power can render the greatest service, followed by those endowed with intellectual power.
Whatever they do, they do under the instructions of those endowed with intellectual and spiritual power.
Social control will have to be in the hands of those who are spiritually elevated, intelligent and brave all at the same time.

paragraphs.text: 5-16. Deshakálapátraeh upayogáh parivarttante te upayogáh pragatishiiláh bhaveyuh.
summary: Deshakálapátraeh upayogáh parivarttante te upayogáh pragatishiiláh bhaveyuh.
paragraphs.sutraRoman: Deshakálapátraeh upayogáh parivarttante te upayogáh pragatishiiláh bhaveyuh
paragraphs.devanagari: देशकालपात्रैः उपयोगाः परिवर्त्तन्ते ते उपयोगाः प्रगतिशीलाः भवेयुः॥
paragraphs.bangla: দেশকালপাত্রৈঃ উপযোগাঃ পরিবর্ত্তন্তে তে উপযোগাঃ প্রগতিশীলাঃ ভবেযুঃ॥

paragraphs.text: [The method of utilization should vary in accordance with changes in time, space and person, and the utilization should be of progressive nature.]
summary: [The method of utilization should vary in accordance with changes in time, space and person, and the utilization should be of progressive nature.

paragraphs.text: Purport: The proper use of any object changes according to changes in time, space and person. Those who cannot understand this simple principle want to cling to the skeletons of the past, and as a result they are rejected by living society. Sentiments based on narrow nationalism, regionalism, ancestral pride, etc., tend to keep people away from this fundamental principle, so they cannot unreservedly accept it as a simple truth. Consequently, after doing indescribable damage to their country, their fellow citizens and themselves, they are compelled to slink away to the backstage.
summary: Purport: The proper use of any object changes according to changes in time, space and person.
Sentiments based on narrow nationalism, regionalism, ancestral pride, etc.
Consequently, after doing indescribable damage to their country, their fellow citizens and themselves, they are compelled to slink away to the backstage.

paragraphs.text: The method of utilization of every object changes according to time, space and person. This has got to be accepted, and after recognizing this fact, people will have to progressively utilize every object and every idea. For instance, the energy which a powerful person utilizes to operate a huge hammer should be utilized through scientific research to operate more than one hammer at a time, instead of wasting the energy to operate just one hammer. In other words, scientific research, guided by progressive ideas, should extract more and more service from the same human potential. It is not a sign of progress to use outdated technology in an age of developed science.
summary: The method of utilization of every object changes according to time, space and person.

For instance, the energy which a powerful person utilizes to operate a huge hammer should be utilized through scientific research to operate more than one hammer at a time, instead of wasting the energy to operate just one hammer.
It is not a sign of progress to use outdated technology in an age of developed science.

paragraphs.text: Society will have to bravely confront different types of obstacles, large or small, that are likely to arise due to the use of various resources and materials created by progressive ideas and developed technology. Through struggle, society will have to move forward towards victory along the path of all-round fulfilment in life.

footnotes.text: ( 1 ) On 13 October 1989 the author gave the discourse “Minimum Requirements and Maximum Amenities” (Proutist Economics, 1992), and instructed that the essential ideas contained in this discourse should be added to the present chapter. These ideas were summarized by the author as follows: “(1) Minimum requirements are to be guaranteed to all. (2) Special amenities are for people of special calibre as per the environmental condition of the particular age. (3) Maximum amenities are to be guaranteed to all, even to those who have no special qualities – to common people of common calibre. Maximum amenities are to be guaranteed to all as per environmental conditions. These amenities are for those of ordinary calibre – the common people, the so-called downtrodden humanity. (4) All three above are never-ending processes, and they will go on increasing according to the collective potentialities. This appendix to our philosophy may be small, but it is of progressive nature and progressive character. It has far-reaching implications for the future.” –Eds.

( 2 ) In 1959 the author gave five principles in English known as the “Five Fundamental Principles of Prout”. They were published as part of the discourse “The Cosmic Brotherhood” in Idea and Ideology. Subsequently, in 1961, the author dictated Ánanda Sútram, whose fifth chapter contains, as we see here, sixteen Sanskrit sútras, or aphorisms. Aphorisms 12 to 16 correspond to the Five Fundamental Principles given earlier in English. In this edition of Ánanda Sútram, the author's original English of each of the Five Fundamental Principles has been printed below the corresponding Sanskrit aphorism. (Though in each case it is the author's English, it has been presented in square brackets because it was not originally given in the context of this book.) What follows every other Sanskrit aphorism in this chapter and other chapters is a translation of the aphorism rendered by the editors. Thus the bracketed English below the Sanskrit in each of Aphorisms 12-16 is not a translation as such. Note that the word samája in Sútra 5-12 is normally translated “society”; “collective body” appears in the English. Parivarttante in Sútra 5-16 is normally translated “does vary” (present indicative); “should vary” appears in the English. –Eds.

paragraphs.devanagari:
स्थूलीभवने निद्रिता सा कुण्डलिनी॥
स्थूलीभवने (7थ चसे) = इन् थे प्रोचेस्स ओफ् च्रुदिफिचतिओन्।
निद्रिता = स्लेएपिङ्ग।
सा = शे।
कुण्डलिनी = चोइलेद् सेर्पेन्तिने॥
paragraphs.bangla:
স্থূলীভবনে নিদ্রিতা সা কুণ্ডলিনী॥
স্থূলীভবনে (7থ চসে) = ইন্ থে প্রোচেস্স ওফ্ চ্রুদিফিচতিওন্।
নিদ্রিতা = স্লেএপিঙ্গ।
সা = শে।
কুণ্ডলিনী = চোইলেদ্ সের্পেন্তিনে॥
paragraphs.oriya:
ସ୍ଥୂଲୀଭଵନେ ନିଦ୍ରିତା ସା କୁଣ୍ଡଲିନୀ॥
ସ୍ଥୂଲୀଭଵନେ (7ଥ ଚସେ) = ଇନ୍ ଥେ ପ୍ରୋଚେସ୍ସ ଓଫ୍ ଚ୍ରୁଦିଫିଚତିଓନ୍।
ନିଦ୍ରିତା = ସ୍ଲେଏପିଙ୍ଗ।
ସା = ଶେ।
କୁଣ୍ଡଲିନୀ = ଚୋଇଲେଦ୍ ସେର୍ପେନ୍ତିନେ॥
paragraphs.punjabi:
ਸ੍ਥੂਲੀਭਵਨੇ ਨਿਦ੍ਰਿਤਾ ਸਾ ਕੁਣ੍ਡਲਿਨੀ॥
ਸ੍ਥੂਲੀਭਵਨੇ (7ਥ ਚਸੇ) = ਇਨ੍ ਥੇ ਪ੍ਰੋਚੇਸ੍ਸ ਓਫ੍ ਚ੍ਰੁਦਿਫਿਚਤਿਓਨ੍।
ਨਿਦ੍ਰਿਤਾ = ਸ੍ਲੇਏਪਿਙ੍ਗ।
ਸਾ = ਸ਼ੇ।
ਕੁਣ੍ਡਲਿਨੀ = ਚੋਇਲੇਦ੍ ਸੇਰ੍ਪੇਨ੍ਤਿਨੇ॥
paragraphs.kannada:
ಸ್ಥೂಲೀಭವನೇ ನಿದ್ರಿತಾ ಸಾ ಕುಣ್ಡಲಿನೀ॥
ಸ್ಥೂಲೀಭವನೇ (7ಥ ಚಸೇ) = ಇನ್ ಥೇ ಪ್ರೋಚೇಸ್ಸ ಓಫ್ ಚ್ರುದಿಫಿಚತಿಓನ್।

paragraphs.text: [In the ultimate state of crudification, the paráshakti lying dormant at Svayambhúliuṋga is called kuńd́alinii (“coiled serpentine”).]
summary: [In the ultimate state of crudification, the paráshakti lying dormant at Svayambhúliuṋga is called kuńd́alinii (“coiled serpentine”).

paragraphs.text: 4-8 Kuńd́alinii sá múliibhútá rńátmiká.
summary: 4-8 Kuńd́alinii sá múliibhútá rńátmiká.

summary: kuńd́alinii = literally “coiled serpentine”; sá = she; múliibhútá = fundamentally; rńátmiká = negative

paragraphs.text: [The kuńd́alinii is the (force of) fundamental negativity.]
summary: [The kuńd́alinii is the (force of) fundamental negativity.

paragraphs.text: 5-1. Varńapradhánatá cakradháráyám.
summary: Varńapradhánatá cakradháráyám.

paragraphs.text: varńa = colour (here, mental colour); pradhánatá = predominance; cakra = “cycle”, social cycle; dháráyám (7th case) = in the flow
summary: varńa = colour (here, mental colour); pradhánatá = predominance; cakra = “cycle”, social cycle; dháráyám (7th case) = in the flow

paragraphs.text: [In the movement of the social cycle, one class is always dominant.]
summary: [In the movement of the social cycle, one class is always dominant.

summary: Cakrakendre sadvipráh cakraniyantrakáh.

paragraphs.text: cakrakendre (7th case) = in the nucleus of the social cycle; sadviprah (pl.) = literally “true vipras”; cakra = cycle; niyantrakáh = controllers
summary: cakrakendre (7th case) = in the nucleus of the social cycle; sadviprah (pl.

paragraphs.text: [Located in the nucleus of the social cycle, sadvipras control the social cycle.]
summary: [Located in the nucleus of the social cycle, sadvipras control the social cycle.

paragraphs.text: 5-3. Shaktisampátena cakragativardhanaḿ krántih.

summary: [Accelerating the movement of the social cycle by the application of force is called “evolution”.

paragraphs.text: tiivra = tremendous, sudden and severe; shakti = force; sampátena (3rd case) = through application; gativardhanaḿ = to accelerate the movement of; viplavah = literally “the flow that inundates everything”, i.e., revolution
summary: tiivra = tremendous, sudden and severe; shakti = force; sampátena (3rd case) = through application; gativardhanaḿ = to accelerate the movement of; viplavah = literally “the flow that inundates everything”, i.

summary: [Accelerating the movement of the social cycle by the application of tremendous force is called “revolution”.

paragraphs.text: 5-5. Shaktisampátena vipariitadháráyáḿ vikrántih.

paragraphs.text: shakti = force; sampátena (3rd case) = through application; vipariita = opposite; dháráyáḿ (7th case) = in the flow; vikrántih = counter-evolution
summary: shakti = force; sampátena (3rd case) = through application; vipariita = opposite; dháráyáḿ (7th case) = in the flow; vikrántih = counter-evolution

paragraphs.text: [Reversing the movement of the social cycle by the application of force is called “counter-evolution”.]
summary: [Reversing the movement of the social cycle by the application of force is called “counter-evolution”.

paragraphs.text: 5-6. Tiivrashaktisampátena vipariitadháráyaḿ prativiplavah.
summary: Tiivrashaktisampátena vipariitadháráyaḿ prativiplavah.

paragraphs.text: tiivra = tremendous; shakti = force; sampátena (3rd case) = through application; vipariita = opposite; dháráyáḿ (7th case) = in the flow; prativiplavah = counter-revolution
summary: tiivra = tremendous; shakti = force; sampátena (3rd case) = through application; vipariita = opposite; dháráyáḿ (7th case) = in the flow; prativiplavah = counter-revolution

paragraphs.text: [Reversing the movement of the social cycle by the application of tremendous force is called “counter-revolution”.]
summary: [Reversing the movement of the social cycle by the application of tremendous force is called “counter-revolution”.

paragraphs.text: 5-7. Púrńávartanena parikrántih.

paragraphs.text: púrńa = full; ávartanena (3rd case) = with the rotation or turning; parikrántih = completion of cyclic movement
summary: púrńa = full; ávartanena (3rd case) = with the rotation or turning; parikrántih = completion of cyclic movement

paragraphs.text: [A complete rotation of the social cycle is called “peripheric evolution”.]
summary: [A complete rotation of the social cycle is called “peripheric evolution”.

summary: vaecitryaḿ = diversity, colourfulness; prákrta = natural, pertaining to: Prakrti (Supreme Operative Principle); dharmah = characteristic, fundamental law; samánaḿ = equal qualitative and quantitative value of two dissimilar objects; na = no, not; bhaviśyati = will be

paragraphs.text: [Diversity, not identity, is the law of nature.]
summary: [Diversity, not identity, is the law of nature.

paragraphs.text: yugasya (6th case) = of an age; sarvanimnaprayojanaḿ = minimum necessities; sarveśáḿ = of all; vidheyam = should be provided

paragraphs.devanagari: तीव्रसङ्घर्षेण चूर्णीभूतानि जडानि चित्ताणु मानसधातुः वा॥
paragraphs.bangla: তীব্রসঙ্ঘর্ষেণ চূর্ণীভূতানি জডানি চিত্তাণু মানসধাতুঃ বা॥
paragraphs.oriya: ତୀଵ୍ରସଙ୍ଘର୍ଷେଣ ଚୂର୍ଣୀଭୂତାନି ଜଡାନି ଚିତ୍ତାଣୁ ମାନସଧାତୁଃ ଵା॥
paragraphs.punjabi: ਤੀਵ੍ਰਸਙ੍ਘਰ੍षੇਣ ਚੂਰ੍ਣੀਭੂਤਾਨਿ ਜਡਾਨਿ ਚਿਤ੍ਤਾਣੁ ਮਾਨਸਧਾਤੁਃ ਵਾ॥
paragraphs.kannada: ತೀವ್ರಸಙ್ಘರ್ಷೇಣ ಚೂರ್ಣೀಭೂತಾನಿ ಜಡಾನಿ ಚಿತ್ತಾಣು ಮಾನಸಧಾತುಃ ವಾ॥

paragraphs.devanagari: महदहंवर्जिते अनग्रसरे जीवदेहे लतागुल्मे केवलं चित्तम्॥
paragraphs.bangla: মহদহংবর্জিতে অনগ্রসরে জীবদেহে লতাগুল্মে কেবলং চিত্তম্॥
paragraphs.oriya: ମହଦହଂଵର୍ଜିତେ ଅନଗ୍ରସରେ ଜୀଵଦେହେ ଲତାଗୁଲ୍ମେ କେଵଲଂ ଚିତ୍ତମ୍॥
paragraphs.punjabi: ਮਹਦਹਂਵਰ੍ਜਿਤੇ ਅਨਗ੍ਰਸਰੇ ਜੀਵਦੇਹੇ ਲਤਾਗੁਲ੍ਮੇ ਕੇਵਲਂ ਚਿਤ੍ਤਮ੍॥
paragraphs.kannada: ಮಹದಹಂವರ್ಜಿತೇ ಅನಗ್ರಸರೇ ಜೀವದೇಹೇ ಲತಾಗುಲ್ಮೇ ಕೇವಲಂ ಚಿತ್ತಮ್॥

paragraphs.text: 1-19. Mahadvarjite anagrasare jiivadehe latágulme cittayuktáham.
summary: Mahadvarjite anagrasare jiivadehe latágulme cittayuktáham

summary: Prágrasare jiive latágulme mánuśe mahadahaḿ cittáni
paragraphs.sutraRoman: Prágrasare jiive latágulme mánuśe mahadahaḿ cittáni
paragraphs.devanagari: प्राग्रसरे जीवे लतागुल्मे मानुषे महदहं चित्तानि॥
paragraphs.bangla: প্রাগ্রসরে জীবে লতাগুল্মে মানুষে মহদহং চিত্তানি॥
paragraphs.oriya: ପ୍ରାଗ୍ରସରେ ଜୀଵେ ଲତାଗୁଲ୍ମେ ମାନୁଷେ ମହଦହଂ ଚିତ୍ତାନି॥
paragraphs.punjabi: ਪ੍ਰਾਗ੍ਰਸਰੇ ਜੀਵੇ ਲਤਾਗੁਲ੍ਮੇ ਮਾਨੁषੇ ਮਹਦਹਂ ਚਿਤ੍ਤਾਨਿ॥
paragraphs.kannada: ಪ್ರಾಗ್ರಸರೇ ಜೀವೇ ಲತಾಗುಲ್ಮೇ ಮಾನುಷೇ ಮಹದಹಂ ಚಿತ್ತಾನಿ॥

paragraphs.text: 1-21. Bhúmávyápte Mahati ahaḿ cittayorprańáshe saguńásthitih savikalpasamádhih vá.
summary: Bhúmávyápte Mahati ahaḿ cittayorprańáshe saguńásthitih savikalpasamádhih vá

paragraphs.devanagari: भूमाव्याप्ते महति अहं चित्तयोर्प्रणाशे सगुणास्थितिः सविकल्पसमाधिः वा॥
paragraphs.bangla: ভূমাব্যাপ্তে মহতি অহং চিত্তযোর্প্রণাশে সগুণাস্থিতিঃ সবিকল্পসমাধিঃ বা॥
paragraphs.oriya: ଭୂମାଵ୍ଯାପ୍ତେ ମହତି ଅହଂ ଚିତ୍ତଯୋର୍ପ୍ରଣାଶେ ସଗୁଣାସ୍ଥିତିଃ ସଵିକଲ୍ପସମାଧିଃ ଵା॥
paragraphs.punjabi: ਭੂਮਾਵ੍ਯਾਪ੍ਤੇ ਮਹਤਿ ਅਹਂ ਚਿਤ੍ਤਯੋਰ੍ਪ੍ਰਣਾਸ਼ੇ ਸਗੁਣਾਸ੍ਥਿਤਿਃ ਸਵਿਕਲ੍ਪਸਮਾਧਿਃ ਵਾ॥
paragraphs.kannada: ಭೂಮಾವ್ಯಾಪ್ತೇ ಮಹತಿ ಅಹಂ ಚಿತ್ತಯೋರ್ಪ್ರಣಾಶೇ ಸಗುಣಾಸ್ಥಿತಿಃ ಸವಿಕಲ್ಪಸಮಾಧಿಃ ವಾ॥

paragraphs.devanagari: विदेहीमानसे न कर्तृत्वं न सुखानि न दुह्खानि॥
paragraphs.bangla: বিদেহীমানসে ন কর্তৃত্বং ন সুখানি ন দুহ্খানি॥
paragraphs.oriya: ଵିଦେହୀମାନସେ ନ କର୍ତୃତ୍ଵଂ ନ ସୁଖାନି ନ ଦୁହ୍ଖାନି॥
paragraphs.punjabi: ਵਿਦੇਹੀਮਾਨਸੇ ਨ ਕਰ੍ਤृਤ੍ਵਂ ਨ ਸੁਖਾਨਿ ਨ ਦੁਹ੍ਖਾਨਿ॥
paragraphs.kannada: ವಿದೇಹೀಮಾನಸೇ ನ ಕರ್ತೃತ್ವಂ ನ ಸುಖಾನಿ ನ ದುಹ್ಖಾನಿ॥

paragraphs.sutraRoman: Vádhá sá yuśamáná shaktih sevyaḿ sthápayati lakśye
paragraphs.devanagari: वाधा सा युषमाना शक्तिः सेव्यं स्थापयति लक्ष्ये॥
paragraphs.bangla: বাধা সা যুষমানা শক্তিঃ সেব্যং স্থাপযতি লক্ষ্যে॥
paragraphs.oriya: ଵାଧା ସା ଯୁଷମାନା ଶକ୍ତିଃ ସେଵ୍ଯଂ ସ୍ଥାପଯତି ଲକ୍ଷ୍ଯେ॥
paragraphs.punjabi: ਵਾਧਾ ਸਾ ਯੁषਮਾਨਾ ਸ਼ਕ੍ਤਿਃ ਸੇਵ੍ਯਂ ਸ੍ਥਾਪਯਤਿ ਲਕ੍ष੍ਯੇ॥
paragraphs.kannada: ವಾಧಾ ಸಾ ಯುಷಮಾನಾ ಶಕ್ತಿಃ ಸೇವ್ಯಂ ಸ್ಥಾಪಯತಿ ಲಕ್ಷ್ಯೇ॥

paragraphs.oriya: ପ୍ରଥମା ଅଵ୍ଯକ୍ତେ ସା ଶିଵାନୀ କେନ୍ଦ୍ରେ ଚ ପରମଶିଵଃ॥
paragraphs.punjabi: ਪ੍ਰਥਮਾ ਅਵ੍ਯਕ੍ਤੇ ਸਾ ਸ਼ਿਵਾਨੀ ਕੇਨ੍ਦ੍ਰੇ ਚ ਪਰਮਸ਼ਿਵਃ॥
paragraphs.kannada: ಪ್ರಥಮಾ ಅವ್ಯಕ್ತೇ ಸಾ ಶಿವಾನೀ ಕೇನ್ದ್ರೇ ಚ ಪರಮಶಿವಃ॥

points.body: Ánanda Sútram means, in part, “aphorisms leading to ánanda, divine bliss”. The sútra form has been valued over the centuries as a powerful tool for communicating a deep philosophy in a condensed, memorable way. The literal meaning of sútra is “thread”, implying that numerous jewels of thought can be strung on a single such thread. In the best traditions of sútra literature, the eighty-five sútras of this book serve, with breathtaking conciseness, as a framework for the entire Ananda Marga ideology.

Removal of one side of the paper jeopardizes the existence of the other. So is the relation of Puruśa [Consciousness] and Prakrti [Operative Principle] in the Cosmic Entity. points.body: The physical sense of the body is telepathized on the mental plate. In other words, the physical sense is awakened in the mental plate due to the reflection that follows the impact of the crude physical waves on the mental plate. Similarly, the sense of every crude object is awakened in the mental plate as soon as the reflection takes place following the impact of the waves of the objects on the mental plate. Identical mental waves hit the soul entity, causing the reflection of those mental waves, and this awakens in the unit a sense of its indivisibility from the soul. If, in the language of philosophy, mental waves, that is, thought, be called thought-waves, then the reflection of the mental waves on the soul-plate will have to be termed telepathic waves. And so in reference to the soul-plate, we may say that it is telepathic to the mind. All mundane objects, crude, subtle or causal, consist in mental waves or thought-waves, and so in the fullest accord with reasoning and logic, we may call the Soul omni-telepathic. It is because of this omni-telepathic Átman that the existences of all mundane objects, visible or invisible, large or small, find their factual substantiation and recognition. Had there been no Átman, the existence of everything would have been in jeopardy.

points.body: Purport: Every object has a material cause and an efficient cause. Over and above these there is also a conjunctive agency linking the upádána kárańa [material cause] with the nimitta kárańa [efficient or instrumental cause]. The determination of the firmness or laxity of the relation of the material cause with the efficient cause depends on the degree of conjunctive functions. In the process of creation, Puruśa is the material factor, and Prakrti is the linking force consummating the relation between the material and the efficient causes. As the efficient cause, Puruśa is the primary factor, and Prakrti is the secondary one.

summary: Puruśa is the all-pervading entity, and so no one else except Him can be the material cause.
Prakrti, not being all-pervading, is sheltered in Puruśa.
In the body of Puruśa, Prakrti can only work as much as She is given opportunity to by Puruśa.
points.body: Puruśa is the all-pervading entity, and so no one else except Him can be the material cause. Prakrti, not being all-pervading, is sheltered in Puruśa. In the body of Puruśa, Prakrti can only work as much as She is given opportunity to by Puruśa. And so, in the science of creation, Puruśa alone as the doer entity is the chief efficient or instrumental cause; and since Prakrti has been posing as the doer with the authority given to Her by Puruśa, She is the subordinate efficient cause. The distortions or expressions which are taking place in the material cause through the efficient cause and which we call worldly manifestations, are effected by the three guńas [attributes or binding principles: sattva, rajah and tamah] of Prakrti. This accounts for Prakrti being the linking force between the efficient cause and the material cause. So the firmness or feebleness of the object-body fully depends upon the degree of the influence of Prakrti.

summary: The role of Puruśa is foremost in all the spheres.

In the process of evolution, Puruśa gives Prakrti the authority to work, and She goes on working.
points.body: The role of Puruśa is foremost in all the spheres. Prakrti only acts to whatever extent Puruśa has authorized or authorizes Her to act. In the process of evolution, Puruśa gives Prakrti the authority to work, and She goes on working. The subtle Puruśa goes on attaining crudity gradually due to the bondage of the three guńas of Prakrti. In the ultimate state of His crudity, Puruśa slowly and gradually keeps shrivelling up the opportunity and liberty of Prakrti previously given to Her, and thus the crudified Puruśa, gradually regaining His subtlety, returns to His own ultimate characteristic state. The flow of manifestations of the Puruśadeha [Cognitive Body] under the binding influence of Prakrti is what we call saiṋcara [extroversion from the subtle to the crude], while the gradual process of liberation that results in the Puruśadeha due to progressive looseness of the bondage is what we call pratisaiṋcara [introversion from the crude to the subtle]. It is now abundantly clear that even though Prakrti is free to make honest use of Her acquired power, the attainment or non-attainment of this power depends on Puruśa, or Citishakti [Cognitive Principle], and so we have to say, Prakrti is but the characteristic of Puruśa Himself – Shaktih Sá Shivasya Shaktih.

points.body: Purport: The existence of any entity is known by the process of its activity, thought or witness-ship, of which witness-ship belongs to Puruśa and the other two substantiating factors primarily belong to Prakrti; and so the fact of Prakrti being the causal entity of the stream of action and thought will be recognized only when She completely identifies herself with objectivity. This appropriation of objectivity by Prakrti depends on Her ever-increasing (saiṋcara) or -decreasing (pratisaiṋcara) influence on Puruśa. Prakrti's manifestation lies in the saiṋcara and pratisaiṋcara processes. In all these manifestations of Prakrti, Puruśa exists not only as the material cause, but as the witness as well, in all states and conditions.

points.body: Purport: The trivalent Prakrti has been apparently crudifying the original Puruśa through Her own binding forces – this is one of the processes of Her activity. Her other process being that by gradually relaxing the influence of Her three attributes on the crude object, She regains the characteristic of Puruśa, thus putting an end to Her binding operation. The first-named process of Prakrti is centrifugal and the other one is centripetal. The Brahma Cakra, or Srśt́i Cakra [Cosmic Cycle], is manifested through the combination of these very centrifugal and centripetal actions. The nucleus of this Cosmic Cycle is indeed the svabháva [characteristic bearing] of Puruśa. The material cause of the entire Brahma Cakra is Puruśa, or Shiva, and we shall call this nucleus Paramashiva or Puruśottama.

As the result of the initial impact of Prakrti on the witnessing Puruśottama, there awakens in Him the sense of existence, which in the language of philosophy is called the Mahattattva [Existential “I”], and the operative force concerned, whereby this Mahattattva comes into being, is called sattvaguńa (the sentient principle) of Prakrti.
(Guńa means “binding principle”.) The second impact of the operative force of Prakrti results in the emergence of the sense of doership or authorship.
points.body: Purport: The object-ward movement or expression of Puruśa from the nucleus of the Brahma Cakra under the influence of Prakrti is called pravrtti (extroversial phase). As the result of the initial impact of Prakrti on the witnessing Puruśottama, there awakens in Him the sense of existence, which in the language of philosophy is called the Mahattattva [Existential “I”], and the operative force concerned, whereby this Mahattattva comes into being, is called sattvaguńa (the sentient principle) of Prakrti. (Guńa means “binding principle”.) The second impact of the operative force of Prakrti results in the emergence of the sense of doership or authorship. This changed expression of Puruśa is called the Ahaḿtattva (Doer “I”), and the operative force concerned is called rajoguńa (the mutative principle) of Prakrti. Finally, through the greater impact of the operative force of Prakrti in the wake of Her successive attacks, comes the crudest objectivity or complete objectivation of Puruśa (the crudest objective counterpart of the subjective Cosmos). This condition of Puruśa is called citta (mind-stuff). The operative force concerned, whereby such objectivation takes place, is called tamoguńa (the static principle) of Prakrti. That is to say, with the onset of pravrtti [desire and attachment], saiṋcara issues right from one and the same Puruśa through the gradual process of the guńas.

points.body: Purport: The excess of vrtti [desire] is pravrtti [attachment or the accelerated momentum of desire]. The recessive or waning momentum of vrtti is nivrtti [detachment or the loss of desire in the introversial phase]. During the centrifugal movement, desire finds its fullest expression in Puruśa under the static influence of Prakrti. The citta entity that comes into play in the body of Puruśa under the static influence of Prakrti, when accepted by the jiivátman [the individual soul or the subjective part of the microcosm] as something perceivable or knowable, appears as the five gross physical elements, ten indriyas [organs] and five tanmátras [sensible and super-sensible inferences or generic essences]. When the attributional flow reaches its finality, then starts the shedding of the guńas – that is to say, Puruśa then keeps contracting the power of Prakrti. The result is that Prakrti, attracted by Puruśa, gets drawn to Puruśottama. Consequently again, the five gross physical elements gradually get metamorphosed into body, vital energy and mind of the unit. Finally the unit mind merges into Puruśottama as the result of shedding of the binding principles. It is because of the merger of the unit mind into its primal cause that the ultimate state of pratisaiṋcara is a non-attributive one. This may be called the dissolution of the individual life.
